title: WorkItem
$comment: Source of the TypeScript twin in frontend/src/types/generated-cases.ts. Edit this, then run `deploy.sh usecase run business-operations types`; the drift test fails until the twin matches.
description: One case: an item in the use case's cases table.

case_id.description: Case identity and the table's sole partition key: {short_id}-{26 base32 chars}, a readable pack prefix and a digest of `key`, so any natural key of any arity gets an id that is legal in a URL, an SQS MessageGroupId, a Memory session id and an AppSync channel segment. Opaque: what the case IS lives in `key`. Built and parsed only through the case_key codec (agent/utils/case_key.py, frontend/src/lib/caseKey.ts).

key.description: The case's natural key in the source system — SAP field name to value. The names are the ones the pack declares (the `source.key` block of packs/<pack_id>/pack.json), but this is a map and so carries no order: DynamoDB does not preserve a map's key order, and a `Scan` returns an AP key declared `SupplierInvoice, FiscalYear` as `FiscalYear, SupplierInvoice`. Anything that renders these values in order reads the order off `source.key` in `GET /registry`, which is an array for that reason. This is what identifies the case: `case_id` is a digest of it, so the record has to carry it back for display, logs, and the GET /cases?key= lookup — none of which depend on the order (`api/cases/index.py` sorts for the filter and re-checks whole-map equality). Any arity: two fields for an AP invoice, three for a material/plant/batch case.

document_number.description: SAP document number (e.g. supplier invoice). A descriptive attribute, not identity: SAP calls and display need it. Optional: a pack keyed on something that is not a document (a material, a cost center) has none. Top-level rather than in `attributes` because a key spec's `as` writes it.

item_id.description: Item identifier within the document. A descriptive attribute, not identity, and top-level for the same reason as document_number.

pack_id.description: Which use case pack this item belongs to; see the PackId definition. The table's pack-status-index is keyed on it.

process_type.description: The process type the case was created with, which routes its first run: the pack's `source.process_type.default` (`invoice_matching`, the triage type, in finance_ops) unless a `source.process_type.rules` entry matched. Written once by the case's producer and never rewritten; the type the agent identified is `exception_type`.

exception_type.description: The exception type the agent identified: the process type of the last exception SOP a run of this case was given, either the SOP it was routed to or one `load_sop` served (an alias recorded as the type it aliases). Written by the agent runtime in the statement that appends that run's trace (agent/utils/case_persistence.py), never through update_case_state, and only for a type the case's own pack maps to an exception SOP: a triage or shared SOP is never recorded (registry.sop_kinds). Absent until a run identifies one; a later run that identifies another replaces it.

test_data.description: Present when the seeder posted the documents this case is about (the console's test data page or `ops.py seed`): its record of the post, copied by the case's producer or by the seeder, never from a request. Absent on every other case.

status_reason.description: Why the case is in its current status, when the status alone does not say. Server-owned and written only by the paths that move a case without the agent asking them to: the invoker when a run stops at a processing limit or exhausts its redrive, and case_persistence when the runtime parks a case itself. Not writable through update_case_state: a model-authored reason would let a run explain away a status the platform assigned it.

disposition.description: What was decided, as opposed to the fact that the case finished: a short snake_case label the agent records when it closes a case — `released`, `rejected_duplicate`, `escalated_to_buyer`. The status says a case is `complete`; only this says what completing it meant, which is why the precedent row a resolved case produces carries it (`agent_knowledge.precedent.disposition`, NOT NULL) and why `get_precedent` returns it as evidence. Model-authored, unlike `status_reason`, and deliberately open rather than an enum: what a disposition can be is a property of the SOP, so an enum here would have to be edited to add a pack. A SOP that names one is what makes it appear — `packs/finance_ops/sops/duplicate_invoice.txt` requires `rejected_duplicate`. Absent where no SOP asked for one; the exemplar builder then derives a mechanical stand-in from the case's own SAP writes rather than recording the constant its status already states.

origin.description: Set to `sap-push` when a sender's typed records made the case, so its key and attributes are what the sender said. The run checks never let a pushed amount lift the approval limit. Absent on a case the poller or a nudge read from SAP itself.

attributes.description: What this case's pack knows about it that the platform does not: the values the pack's `field_map` pulled out of SAP (`source.field_map` in `packs/<pack_id>/pack.json`), under the names that config chose. Open by design — an AP case carries `amount` and `supplier_number`, a material case carries `plant` and `base_unit`, and neither shape appears here, so adding a pack costs a config file rather than a schema edit and a regenerated type in two languages. Scalars only: these are display and prompt values, and a nested object would reach a label as `[object Object]`. The names are checked at build time against the pack config that writes them (business_operations/validate_packs.py).

ticket_id.description: Related demo ticket ID while the case awaits a supervised response.

ticket_response_type.description: The response_type of the ticket in ticket_id, stamped with it by demo_create_ticket (tickets_tool/handler.py), so a list tells a case waiting on an approval from one waiting on an answer without reading its ticket. inquiry_sent_at cannot: it is stamped on every move to awaiting_human_input.

inquiry_sent_at.description: ISO timestamp of the outbound inquiry that put the case into awaiting_human_input. Server-owned: stamped by the case management tool on entry to that status and cleared on leaving it, never taken from model-authored updates — it is what lets the handover claim 'waiting 6d' rather than 'last activity 6d'.

action_log.description: Append-only audit trail: one entry per update_case_state call (case_management/handler.py) and one per human decision on the case (api/layer/python/decisions.py), each written by the server, never taken from the caller.

ttl.description: DynamoDB TTL (epoch seconds). For seeded synthetic cases only, so they self-clean; a real case never carries one, and the model cannot write it.

ratings.description: Human ratings of the resolution, keyed by the rater's `sub`. One per rater; rating again replaces your own. Written only by `PUT /cases/{case_id}/rating`.

agent_traces.description: Historical agent thought-process traces, one per invocation.

cost_summary.description: Per-case accumulated agent cost. Written by agent/utils/case_persistence.py.

traces_dropped.description: Count of oldest traces evicted by the per-case trace cap, so the UI can state that history was thinned rather than thinning it silently.

live_run.description: The run currently streaming on this case. Written every ~2s while it runs and REMOVEd in the same update that appends the finished trace. Absent means no run is in flight; an updated_at older than 60s means the run was interrupted.

decision_options.description: The outcomes a person may choose between while the case waits on a decision, each with the exact write it would make. Written only by update_case_state, in the update that sets awaiting_human_input; any other status write, and the invoker as a run starts, removes it. A decision route takes one option's id and approves that option's write and nothing else (api/layer/python/decision_options.py).

PackId.description: Which use case pack this item belongs to. Names a directory under packs/ whose pack.json claims the process types and declares the `source` block the poller reads — and the build-time validator checks the pack is coherent, which a hand-maintained enum could not: it would happily list a pack that does not exist. Open by design, for the same reason as Trigger: a use case is a directory of configuration, so adding one should cost a directory rather than a schema edit and a regenerated type in two languages. Open is not unvalidated — the pattern is a lower snake_case identifier, which is what makes the value legal as a directory name, an entitlement subject, and the readable half of a case_id. A value that names no published pack still validates and renders as its humanised id.

CaseStatus.description: `error` is terminal-until-retried: the SOPs and skill prompts instruct the agent to write it when a tool call fails irrecoverably, so it must be a first-class state rather than a value the UI silently renders as 'Detected'.

action.description: Action name the caller supplied, e.g. sap_updated, invoice_released.

actor.description: The deciding human's `sub`, from the authorizer. Human decisions only.

actor_display.description: That human's display claim (email first) at the time.

approved_write.description: sha256 of the write the approver saw: the chosen option's write, or else the latest proposed_write in the case's traces. Absent when there was none.

consumed_by_run.description: On an approval: the run whose grant carried it, set by the invoker as it writes that grant. An approval authorizes one run, so a second run on it is unapproved.

option.description: On a decision that chose one of the case's decision_options: its id.

option_label.description: That option's label, as the person saw it.

option_write.description: That option's write, copied by the decision route as the person saw it; approved_write is its sha256. The invoker builds the run's grant from it. Absent for an option that makes no write.

outcome.description: Invocation result: complete, stopped, cancelled, error, disconnected.

sop_version.description: Version the injected SOP declared in its own header, read at resolve_skill time. Names the authority this run actually followed, which a precedent row citing the case must reproduce even after the SOP is revised.

sop_key.description: The SOP object key `sop_version` was read from — the document this run was given, so a reader of the case can open the text it was governed by (the `/packs?doc=` link behind a quoted clause). Absent on a run whose SOP did not load, and on every run persisted before this was recorded. Names the *injected* SOP only: `sop_baseline` also accumulates whatever `load_sop`/`search_sap_sops` returned and keeps no per-document provenance, so a quote lifted from a discovered SOP still resolves here — which is why the UI offers this as 'the SOP this run was given' and never as where a given quote came from.

sop_version_id.description: The S3 VersionId of the SOP bytes this run was given. `sop_version` is typed by the author; this names exactly what the run read, in a bucket that denies version deletes.

exception_type.description: The exception type this run identified, when it did: the case's `exception_type` as this run set it. Absent on a run that stayed in triage or a shared SOP.

intent.description: `ask` on a conversation turn (`POST /runs` without `intent: process`), which withheld every tool that changes SAP, a case, a ticket or sends mail. Absent on a run that could write: Process, a resume after a decision or a reply, a queued run.

initiator.description: who this run acted for — the human's subject for an interactive run, the machine principal for a queued one. Persisted so a SAP write made during the run is attributable from the case alone.

correlation_id.description: The AG-UI run id this trace came from, so the live turn a reader is already rendering from `live_run` can be deduped against the stored trace. Different value from trace_id, which is minted at write time.

estimated_cost_usd.description: Cost of this invocation alone. `cost_summary` on the case is the running total across invocations.

verifier_calls.description: One entry per write-verifier call this invocation made. Its cost is inside `estimated_cost_usd`; its tokens are not in the token fields above, which are the agent's.

reason.description: The verifier's one sentence, or why it gave no usable verdict — every failure is a disagree.

function_name.description: The function import's name, trimmed and upper-cased; empty for an odata_update.

write.description: What the write does by the guards' classification: the function name, RELEASE for an odata_update (it clears the payment block), CANCEL for a reversal. What the benchmark grades against.

timed_out.description: No answer in time. Amazon Bedrock may still have billed it, so the zero cost is a lower bound.

Trigger.description: Which transport initiated an agent invocation. Open by design: transport is a detail, mapping is the contract, so a fourth transport costs a handler and a registry row rather than a schema edit and a regenerated type. A value no transport registers still validates and renders as its humanised id. Open is not unvalidated — the pattern is lower kebab-case, single hyphens, no trailing hyphen, so an id that reaches a label or a log line is one somebody chose.

tool_call_id.description: SDK toolUseId. Joins a stream-folded segment to the evidence the AfterToolCallEvent hook extracted.

status.description: ToolResult.status as reported by the SDK. On the segment rather than inside evidence because it is SDK-native, not derived.

evidence.description: Structured provenance for this tool step. Absent on any trace stored before structured evidence was added.

Evidence.description: Deterministic provenance for one tool call. Only `kind` is required — an unknown tool falls through to `computation` with no source rather than failing.

at.description: ISO timestamp of the tool call.

op.description: sap_write only — the three write shapes do not render as the same kind of diff.

fields.description: Field values read or written. The timeline renders these, never model prose.

clauses_retrieved.description: sop_lookup only — numbered clauses found in the retrieved SOP text. A human locator, not a verification key: most SOPs carry no numbers, so `citation` is what grades.

citation.description: notification and case_update only — the SOP sentence the agent quoted, checked against the text this run was given.

sap_result.description: sap_write only — SAP's own answer, which `authz` cannot state: a refused write is `permitted` too, because Cedar did allow the call to be made. Absent when the provider returned no `success` flag.

truncated.description: True when the tool_input or tool_result preview hit its size budget.

proposed_write.description: notification only — the write the agent is asking permission to make. The one model-supplied key in an otherwise deterministic model, so its `current` values are verified client-side against the run's reads rather than trusted.

SapResult.description: What the provider said happened, as distinct from what policy allowed. The SAP MCP wrapper reports a rejected write as a *successful tool call* carrying `success: false`, so this is the only thing that separates a write that landed from one SAP refused.

accepted.description: The wrapper's own `success` flag. False means SAP refused the write — the case may still have reached a completed status, because the agent is free to misread the refusal.

message.description: The provider's message, truncated. Carries SAP's stated reason on a refusal.

Citation.description: A quoted SOP sentence and whether it is present in the text the run was given. Absent when the agent quoted nothing gradeable — which is a different state from quoting something absent.

quote.description: The span as the agent wrote it, before normalization.

verified.description: False means the span is not in what the agent was shown. It is NOT on its own proof the SOP was violated — a compliant agent that paraphrases lands here too, so the render must never present it as one.

section.description: The number of the SOP clause the quote starts in, as the SOP numbers it (`2.2`, `1.2a`): the nearest clause marker above the quote in the text it verified against (agent/utils/evidence.py, `section_of`). Null when the quote is not verified, sits before the first clause, the SOP numbers nothing, or it was found only in a retrieval chunk whose line breaks were collapsed. Absent on a trace recorded before it existed; read that as null.

ProposedWrite.description: A write declared as structured intent at escalation time, so an approval can render as a diff instead of prose.

op.description: Shares the record half's discriminator — a proposal and a record describe the same three write shapes.

current.description: Absent on a create, and absent whenever the agent did not read the value in this run.

EvidenceKind.description: Drives the timeline's row rendering, so the UI never pattern-matches tool names.

EvidenceSource.description: Where a value came from in SAP.

EvidenceAuthz.description: The authorization facts that are actually available. The matched Cedar policy id is not obtainable from the Gateway.

mode.description: The deployment's Cedar mode: OFF (not enabled) and LOG_ONLY refuse nothing, ENFORCE does. The run checks refuse in every mode.

outcome.description: Absent when a call failed for a non-authorization reason.

CostSummary.description: Per-case accumulated agent cost and token counts, summed across every invocation.

LiveRun.description: A snapshot of the run in flight, so a tab that opens or reloads mid-run renders the turn instead of a gap. Best-effort and self-expiring: nothing sweeps it, so a stale updated_at is the only interruption signal there is.

run_id.description: AG-UI run id. Recorded on the stored trace as correlation_id, which is what a reader dedupes the live turn against — the trace's own trace_id is a different value.

prompt.description: The prompt as sent, same as AgentTrace.prompt — a reader strips the client's scaffolding the same way.

updated_at.description: Bumped on every throttled write. Older than `x-stale-after-seconds` and the run is gone.

segments_dropped.description: Segments trimmed from the front by the 40-segment cap. Absent when nothing was dropped.

UserRating.description: Case-level resolution quality rating from a human reviewer.

name.description: The rater's display claim (email first) when they rated.

at.description: ISO timestamp of when the rating was submitted.

comment.description: Optional comment explaining the rating, at most 5000 characters.

author.description: Set when the rater may author the case's pack. Only such a rater's comment on a negative rating becomes a lesson (exemplar builder).

post_id.description: `<UTC second>#<8 hex>`, the seeder's record of the post.

posted_by.description: The console caller's name from their token, or what `ops.py seed` said about itself.

preset.description: The label of the seed preset the inputs started from, when they did.

expected.description: What the pack's checker and this stack's limits said the case should end as, when posted; null for a pack with no checker.

TestDataMark.description: A seed the seeder recorded, as the case it made carries it.

set_id.description: sha256 of the options' canonical JSON, first 16 hex characters. A decision is recorded only while the case still offers the set it chose from.

effect.description: One line, at most 240 characters, on what happens when this option is chosen.

write.description: The exact write this option makes. Absent for an outcome that makes none.
